Chippi mockup: Settings › Notifications

For Travis's approval. Studio Rack, DESIGN.md tokens. Structure from Karl's notifications research; the Keep awake group is illustrative.

01

Notifications page

  • Sidebar: new Notifications item with a bell, after Island & pet. The Downloads organizer page drops its own Notifications grid (§5 Notices already moves it here).
  • Destinations: two Surface tiles, Windows and Island, each with a neutral 32px icon chip and a switch. Both start on. Island here means island notices only; the island itself and its Status activities are untouched.
  • Groups: one per installed feature that declares events, in Features hub order. A Label eyebrow carries the feature name, and the Windows and Island column headers sit on the same line, so there is no extra header row. Rows use the themed checkbox (same grid as the approved module page, 120px columns). Accessible names read "Downloads organizer, Held, Windows".
  • Defaults: Organized: Island. Ready to review: Island. Held and Failed: Windows and Island. Archive imported: Windows.
  • Keep awake › Timer ended is illustrative only, a future event drawn to prove the pattern (Island on, Windows off). It is not in scope for Phase 2.
  • No description under the title, and no numbers on this page, so no mono beyond the version string.
Dark · default · 1160 × 720
02

Windows off, backend unavailable

  • Off: turning Windows off dims the Windows column in every group to .45 and puts "Off · choices kept" under the tile title. The boxes keep their state and stay editable: hover brings a box back to full strength (Archive imported shows it), and Island keeps working.
  • Unavailable: when the Windows backend is known to be unavailable, an amber status line sits under the tiles: amber dot, Caption text. It does not claim Focus or Do not disturb, because the backend can't report those. Choices stay editable. The line shows whether Windows is on or off.
Dark · Windows off · backend unavailable · hover on a dimmed box
03

Light

  • Same page with the light tokens. In light, the unavailable line's text uses #8A4B00 and its dot stays Signal Amber, per §2.
